one_liner: Rust reimplementation of GNU find, xargs, locate and updatedb aiming at drop-in compatibility; never timed against GNU find.
what_it_does: Provides find, xargs, locate and updatedb binaries that follow GNU findutils command-line syntax and behaviour, built with cargo and also usable as a library through entry points such as findutils::find::find_main with an injectable Dependencies trait (output writer, clock, confirmation prompt). The stated goal is a full drop-in replacement for the GNU commands; progress is tracked by running the GNU and bfs test suites.
how_it_is_fast: It does not claim to be faster and no speed technique is documented. Traversal is a single-threaded depth-first walk through the walkdir crate, -regex matching uses the Rust regex crate with onig (Oniguruma bindings) also in the dependency list, and release builds use fat LTO, codegen-units=1 and panic=abort. Parallel traversal (#112, open since 2021) and a metadata and user/group-name cache (#430, open since 2024) are the only performance ideas on the tracker.
when_to_use: You want a memory-safe find/xargs/locate/updatedb that follows GNU syntax, for example alongside uutils coreutils on a Rust-based userland.
Windows, macOS, Linux or wasm32-wasip1 targets where GNU findutils is unavailable or awkward to ship; CI builds all four.
Embedding find semantics in a Rust program through find_main and the Dependencies trait, with output sent to your own writer.
Scripts that rely on find expression syntax (-prune, -printf, -regex, -size) and are covered by the passing part of the GNU test suite.
when_not_to_use: As a speed upgrade over GNU find: no comparison exists, traversal is single-threaded, and the project's benchmarks measure only its own code.
When exact GNU compatibility matters: the GNU test suite shows 425 of 495 tests passing and 69 failing, and the bfs suite 274 of 317 passing and 37 failing (findutils-tracking, 2026-10-10).
Large-tree searches where a parallel walker helps; hunt, fd or ignore-based walkers are the measured options.
Pure-Rust or minimal-dependency builds: it pulls in clap, chrono, nix, uucore, walkdir, regex and onig, the last binding the C Oniguruma library.

integration.form: crate with binaries (find, xargs, locate, updatedb) and a library API
integration.dependencies: argmax, chrono, clap, faccess, nix, onig (Oniguruma C library bindings), regex, uucore, walkdir, itertools, thiserror; rustix on WASI
integration.platforms: Linux, macOS and Windows tested in CI; wasm32-wasip1 build checked in CI
integration.thread_safety: not documented (command-line tools; the library entry point takes a Dependencies object holding a RefCell writer)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same command names and GNU syntax, but 69 GNU test-suite failures and 37 bfs test-suite failures remain as of 2026-10-10

gotchas: The repo's Criterion benches (benches/find_bench.rs and siblings) build a synthetic tree and call find_main with output sent to io::sink, and CodSpeed runs them in simulation mode; they track regressions in uutils itself and contain no GNU find baseline, so they cannot support a faster-than-GNU claim.
The repository Cargo.toml is at 0.11.0 while crates.io's latest release is 0.10.0 (2026-08-03), so cargo install findutils gives an older build than main.

Every file entry goes through a single-threaded walkdir walk; issue #430 (open) says file metadata is fetched repeatedly and uid/gid-to-name lookups are not cached, which costs most on -user, -group and -printf heavy expressions.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over hunt or walkdir/ignore-based walkers only when GNU find syntax and behaviour matter more than speed; hunt (12.31x on a first-match search) and walkdir in dkorunic/bench_walk (about 1.3x over system find) are the catalogued entries with measured wins over GNU find, and this project has none.
verified_claims_summary: No speed measurement against GNU find exists: the README compares only GNU and bfs test-suite pass rates, the benches time uutils find alone with output discarded, and searches of the issue tracker and the web found no uutils-versus-GNU timing.
status_note: Actively maintained official uutils project (MIT, commits through 2026-10-12, crates.io 0.10.0 with about 21,000 downloads) that is a compatibility replacement rather than a performance pick; it stays at tier D on record only because it was proposed as faster than GNU find.
